# oauth

Cluster OAuth: htpasswd, OpenID Connect and LDAP identity providers, token lifetimes and a cluster-admin group

Guide: https://policystk.io/elements/oauth/

Stability: preview ([Compatibility](https://policystk.io/reference/compatibility/#element-stability))

```yaml
stack:
  oauth:
    enabled: true
```

## Settings

The element owns OAuth cluster: an identity provider or setting not set here is removed from it, including providers and login page templates added by hand. Hosted control plane guests skip every object: set identity providers on the HostedCluster's spec.configuration.oauth.

Under `stack.oauth.config`. Maps merge across layers; lists are replaced whole.

| Key | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `identityProviders` | Identity provider name: {type, mappingMethod, secret, enabled, ...}. type is HTPasswd, OpenID or LDAP. mappingMethod is claim (default), lookup or add. secret is a Secret in the hub's policy namespace, copied to openshift-config as oauth-&lt;name>, holding key htpasswd (HTPasswd, required), clientSecret (OpenID, required) or bindPassword (LDAP, with bindDN). OpenID also takes clientID and issuer (https://, both required), claims {preferredUsername, name, email, groups}, extraScopes and extraAuthorizeParameters. LDAP takes url (ldap:// or ldaps://, required), bindDN, insecure and attributes {id (required), preferredUsername, name, email}. OpenID and LDAP take ca, a PEM CA bundle, written to ConfigMap oauth-&lt;name>-ca. enabled: false removes the provider. The name is 1-50 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens and appears in every user's identity, so keep it. The login page lists providers by name. The layer that turns the element on fills it | `{}` |
| `clusterAdmins` | Users in Group oauth-cluster-admins, which ClusterRoleBinding oauth-cluster-admins binds to ClusterRole cluster-admin. Empty writes neither; emptying it later leaves both as last written | `[]` |
| `accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds` | Lifetime of an access token in seconds; 0 is the OAuth server default, 86400 (24h). spec.tokenConfig.accessTokenMaxAgeSeconds | `0` |
| `accessTokenInactivityTimeout` | A token unused this long stops working: a duration such as 15m or 1h30m, at least 300s. Empty never times out. spec.tokenConfig.accessTokenInactivityTimeout | `''` |

## Policies

`<cluster>` is the ManagedCluster name, or hubName on the hub. `global.remediationAction: inform` overrides every action below.

Standards: NIST SP 800-53. Controls: IA-2 Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users), AC-2 Account Management, AC-12 Session Termination. Categories: IA Identification and Authentication, AC Access Control.

### Policy `config`

`config-oauth-<cluster>`: Identity providers, token lifetimes and the cluster-admin group.

| Template | Action | Severity | Renders | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `config-oauth` | enforce | high | [oauth](converters/config/oauth.yaml) (mustonlyhave) | OAuth cluster, the Secrets and CA bundles it reads, and the cluster-admin Group and binding |
| `config-oauth-ready` | inform (always) | high | [oauth-ready](converters/config/oauth-ready.yaml) | Reports NonCompliant until the authentication ClusterOperator is Available and not Degraded |
